## Working session summary

Pushed to PR #805 (https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/805).

**Evidence collected** into `dev/log/issues/804/pulls/805/` — both failing runs on `8b5acee` (`--log-failed` logs + job metadata + run list) plus `README.md` and `analysis.md` (timeline, R1–R10 requirement list, root causes, solution plans).

**Two concrete failures, root-caused:**

1. **CI/CD Pipeline — false positive that blocks every release.** `scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs:245` requires the trailing 3-release weighted self-hosting percentage to never decrease. The ledger shows `v0.300.0` was an outlier (69.56% per-release → 32.68% trailing), so *any* normal release now fails: `self-hosting ratchet would fall from 32.68% to 19.19%`. A monotonic ratchet over a noisy moving average is unsatisfiable by construction. Proposed: a deliberately-raised `ratchet_floor` (coverage-floor model) + warn-unless-`enforce` escape hatch + move the ledger write out of the release-blocking step.

2. **Desktop Release macOS (x64 + arm64).** `codesign` fails on the bundled `Google Chrome for Testing Framework.framework` with *"unsealed contents present in the root directory of an embedded framework"*. I confirmed the #798 ignore fix (`46aa1dd7`) **is** an ancestor of the failing SHA, that our custom hook *is* invoked, and that `@electron/osx-sign@1.3.3` does support function `ignore` entries — yet the log has zero `Skipped...` lines, so the predicate never fired. The logs can't discriminate between the three remaining hypotheses (wrong app-path field / wrong CWD / dropped ignore entry), so per your instruction I added **opt-in debug output** (`FORMAL_AI_MACOS_SIGN_DEBUG=1`, default off, already set by the workflow) logging the option keys, CWD, resolved app path, ignore root, and a per-path SKIP/sign verdict. Existing tests still pass.

3. Also noted: the aggregation job publishes `SHA256SUMS.txt` *before* checking target completeness, so a partial manifest reaches the release page.

Not yet done (tracked in `analysis.md` §4): the file-by-file comparison against the three `link-foundation` templates, the `continue-on-error`/`|| true` false-negative audit, and filing upstream template issues.
